items.stem: A Kotlin function calls a Java method returning String with no nullability annotation. What is the type of the result in Kotlin?

options.text: A platform type, which Kotlin does not null-check at compile time
options.rationale: Correct: platform types defer the null decision to the developer; a null can slip through.
Kotlin cannot guarantee non-null for an unannotated Java return.

options.text: A compile error until you annotate the Java method
options.rationale: Kotlin compiles; it treats it as a platform type.
It is a platform type, not forced to the nullable form.

items.explanation: Correct: platform types defer the null decision to the developer; a null can slip through.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Kotlin structured concurrency are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Cancelling a parent scope cancels its child coroutines
options.rationale: Correct: structured concurrency propagates cancellation down the scope.

options.text: A suspend function suspends without blocking the underlying thread
options.rationale: Correct: suspension frees the thread to do other work.

options.text: launch returns the coroutine's result value directly
options.rationale: launch returns a Job; async returns a Deferred that holds the result.

options.text: Coroutines always run on a new OS thread each
options.rationale: Many coroutines are multiplexed onto a small dispatcher thread pool.

items.explanation: Correct: structured concurrency propagates cancellation down the scope.

items.stem: A data class User(val name: String, val roles: MutableList<String>) is copied with copy(). What is true of the copy's roles list?

options.text: It references the same mutable list as the original
options.rationale: Correct: copy() is shallow; the MutableList reference is shared.

options.text: It is a deep, independent copy of the list
options.rationale: copy() does not deep-copy nested mutable fields.

options.text: It is null because copy() drops collections
options.rationale: copy() preserves all properties, including the list.
The field type is still MutableList; copy() does not change types.

items.explanation: Correct: copy() is shallow; the MutableList reference is shared.
